answer: Each identity lists one service on an atlas directory, on one willow branch aisle, sealed with a quartz seal bound to its key. The aisle fee rises with occupancy: the kth listing on one aisle pays 30+3(k-1) credits, so the 1000th pays 3027, and 1000 fakes on one aisle pay 1528500 in fees plus 60000 bonds at risk. An honest identity pays 30 once, locks 60 once, and recovers the bond after a clean epoch. Anyone can recompute the aisle count; a rented listing fails because its quartz seal key never matches that willow aisle's work receipts, so the atlas burns the bond and strikes the listing.
